title: When can a lithium-ion cell design search trust a reduced battery model (SPMe) instead of the full DFN model?
lede: research programme on fidelity-aware Li-ion electrode design; milestone 5f: on 4 cells with fresh designs, reading the answer from DFN-verified designs returns the DFN best in all 120 trials and SPMe's early stops re-solve to within 0.2% of DFN; a pilot switch to all-DFN misses on Ai2020 (H46 refuted), but the rule never costs more than 12% over all-DFN on 11 pools and saves 49 to 64% on six; milestone 5e: pre-registered on two new cells, the two-part SPMe trust rule finds all 9 mis-scored designs on Chen2020 (including the DFN-best, which SPMe ranks 16th) for 23% of the pool in DFN runs, but its answer step lands 1.3% short on Marquis2019 by comparing DFN with biased SPMe scores; reading the answer from verified designs fixes it; milestone 5d: SPMe's early solver stops are PyBaMM's default tolerance (all 6 finish at rtol 1e-6 and then score within 0.3% of DFN), while its outright failures are structural (its salt concentration goes negative in the first discharge in 59 of 61, and no solver setting yields a usable score; pre-registered H38 to H41 supported); milestone 5c: on two more PyBaMM cells (Mohtat2020, NCA_Kim2011) SPMe mis-scores designs in two ways, salt depletion (its minimum salt ratio ranks those at AUC 0.995 or better on every cell) and solver stops that PyBaMM returns as partial runs (all 6 of Mohtat2020's, invisible to the salt flag; pre-registered H33 and H34 refuted); flagging both, then verifying with DFN from the most depleted design up until three sound ones, finds every mis-scored design on five cells with fewer DFN runs than a cut-off fitted to 8 random DFN runs (post hoc); milestone 5b: on two more PyBaMM cells (Ecker2015, Ai2020) SPMe's own minimum salt ratio still ranks the designs it mis-scores (AUC 0.995) but the cut-off tuned on OKane2022 misclassifies 20.3% on Ai2020 (best cut-off 0.33, not 0.07), the 10-cycle-beats-100-cycle SPMe effect vanishes, and 2-cycle SPMe or DFN screens still beat GP-EI on all three cells (within 1.3x of the fastest method); milestone 5a: pre-registered on 128 fresh designs, a 10-cycle SPMe screen reaches the DFN-best design in 123 s on pools of 64 against GP-EI's 220 s (p = 2e-6), SPMe's 10-cycle ranking beats its own 100-cycle one (Spearman 0.67 vs 0.58), and 15 search methods rank the same as on the old designs (0.92); the cheap-start co-kriging search beats GP-EI everywhere but trails the best screen on small pools; milestone 3 part 2b: SPMe's error follows -ln of its own minimum salt ratio (cross-validated error halved, 21.3 to 11.3 Wh/kg), but that location neither plans its DFN cost (2 of 4 cells within 2x) nor beats a simple flag as an online correction (528 vs 418 s); post hoc, a plain 10-cycle SPMe screen reaches the DFN-best design in 123 s on pools of 64 and 172 s on 96, faster than GP-EI (220 s) and every earlier screen (exploratory); milestone 4b: multi-fidelity Bayesian optimisation by co-kriging, started as usual from five random full DFN runs, is slower than plain GP-EI (205 vs 220 s on pools of 64, 267 vs 220 s on 96) and than screening with a cheap model, while the same search started from ten 2-cycle DFN runs keeps pace with the best screen at every pool size (144 s at 64, 174 s at 96; exploratory); milestone 3 part 2a: treating a cheap model's error as independent noise gives an exact expected count of full DFN runs, which plans screen-versus-GP-EI right on 14 of 16 pool sizes (worst-case bound: 8) but cannot rank SPMe, whose errors sit on particular designs; milestone 3: a proved bound shows a cheap screen's cost in full DFN runs is bounded by its residual after an affine fit, which ranks 11 screens at Spearman 0.72 (raw error -0.07), and SPMe's residual tracks its own salt depletion (-0.82); milestone 4: replaying 12 searches on the cached benchmark, screening every candidate with the plain SPM or a 2-cycle DFN run reaches a design within 1% of the DFN best about 30% faster than GP-EI on DFN (153 to 168 s vs 220 s on pools of 64), the 10-cycle DFN screen is slower (253 s) and GP-EI catches up by 96 designs; milestone 2: a 10-cycle DFN run ranks designs by 100-cycle DFN energy at Spearman 0.96 against 0.64 for 100-cycle SPMe at the same cost; milestone 1: SPMe's own minimum salt concentration flags the designs it mis-scores (AUC 0.997) (modelled, PyBaMM OKane2022, stack level)
summary: Milestone 5f (a pilot switch and a verified answer step) tests, on 64 fresh designs on each of Mohtat2020, Ai2020, NCA_Kim2011 and Ecker2015 (515 runs), whether 8 SPMe runs plus 2 DFN runs can tell when to skip SPMe and run DFN on everything, and whether verifying the leading design until it is DFN-scored returns the DFN best. The answer step does, in all 120 replayed trials; all 3 early SPMe stops re-solve at tight tolerance to within 0.2% of DFN; recall stays 1.00. The switch fails its test: on Ai2020, where all-DFN is 11.6% cheaper, it fires in 20% of trials, because a salt cut-off of 0.10 misses mis-scored designs with minimum salt ratio up to 0.32. Across 11 cell pools the rule never costs more than 12% over all-DFN and saves 49 to 64% on six, so the recommendation is to run the rule every time. The switch constants were chosen on a post hoc replay of the seven committed cells. Milestone 5e (the rule on new cells) fixes in advance the two-part rule from 5c and 5d (re-solve early SPMe stops at tight tolerance; DFN-verify failed runs, then the rest in ascending minimum salt ratio, until three sound) and runs it on 64 fresh designs on each of two cells it was not built on, Marquis2019 and Chen2020 (256 runs). On Chen2020 it verifies all 9 mis-scored designs in 15 DFN runs (23% of the pool), among them the DFN-best design, which SPMe scores 23% low and ranks 16th; Marquis2019 has no mis-scored design and costs 4 runs. The planned answer step lands 1.3% below the DFN best on Marquis2019 because it compares verified DFN scores with SPMe scores that run 1 to 6% high at the top; taking the best verified design instead (chosen after the verdicts) reaches the DFN best on both cells. No run stopped early, so the re-solve step is untested. Milestone 5d (why SPMe fails) re-solves, pre-registered, every SPMe run on the committed benches that failed outright (61: NCA_Kim2011 49, OKane2022 12) or stopped early (6, Mohtat2020) under four solver and mesh variants, with 24 completed runs as controls (455 runs). Tight tolerances (rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-8, IDAKLU or CasADi) finish all 6 early stops, which then score within 0.3% of DFN; more Newton iterations finish none. No setting gives any of the 61 outright failures a usable score: in 59 SPMe’s linearised salt concentration goes below zero in the first discharge (median −8% of initial), the charge step has no valid start, and PyBaMM discards the run. So stops are re-solved, failures go to DFN. All four hypotheses supported; V0 reproduces all 91 committed runs. Milestone 5c (setting the cut-off on a new cell) compares, pre-registered, a trust-flag cut-off fitted to 8 random DFN runs with verifying designs in ascending order of SPMe’s minimum salt ratio until three sound ones in a row, on the three earlier cells and two new PyBaMM cells, Mohtat2020 and NCA_Kim2011 (64 Sobol designs each, 256 runs). On Mohtat2020 both fail (recall 0.00 and 0.17; H33, H34 and H37 refuted): its 6 mis-scored designs are SPMe runs whose solver stopped part-way (cycles 3 to 90), returned by PyBaMM as normal solutions, with no salt depletion. Among SPMe runs that finish, r_min ranks the mis-scored designs at AUC 0.995 or better on every cell that has any. Flagging early stops as well (post hoc), bottom-up verification finds every mis-scored design on all five cells with 16%, 95%, 6%, 14% and 88% of the pool sent to DFN (mis-scored shares 13%, 89%, 2%, 9%, 81%), always fewer than the 8-run calibration (23% to 98%). Milestone 5b (transfer) runs the trust flag and 9 frozen search methods, pre-registered, on two more PyBaMM parameter sets, Ecker2015 and Ai2020 (64 Sobol designs each, 384 runs, current scaled to the same areal density). SPMe's minimum salt ratio ranks the designs it mis-scores at AUC 0.995 on Ai2020 (57 of 64 mis-scored), but the OKane2022 cut-off r ≤ 0.07 misclassifies 20.3% there (best cut-off 0.33; H2 refuted); SPMe@10 no longer ranks DFN better than SPMe@100 (−0.01 and −0.11); the methods' ordering transfers (Spearman 0.73, 0.70), and the 2-cycle SPMe and DFN screens stay within 1.3× of the fastest method on all three cells while GP-EI is 1.9 to 3.7×. Cells are design-space variants (5% inactive rule, borrowed degradation parameters), not the published cells. Milestone 5a (fresh designs) re-tests, unchanged and pre-registered, the post-hoc winners of parts 2b and 4b on 128 new Sobol designs (384 PyBaMM runs, same parameter set). On pools of 64 the whole-pool 10-cycle SPMe screen reaches a design within 1% of the DFN best in 122.9 s against GP-EI's 220.4 s and the SPM@2 screen's 205.0 s (both p < 0.001); SPMe@10 ranks 100-cycle DFN at Spearman 0.668 against 0.575 for SPMe@100; the 15 methods' medians correlate at 0.924 across the two design sets. Cheap-start MF-UCB co-kriging beats GP-EI at every pool size but is 1.36× and 1.71× the best screen at 16 and 32 designs (refuted), and is fastest at 96. A 2- or 10-cycle SPMe screen stays within 1.4× of the fastest method at every pool size on both sets (descriptive). Same parameter set and protocol: transfer to other cells is untested. Milestone 3 part 2b (where SPMe errs) models SPMe's residual against 100-cycle DFN as a function of SPMe's own minimum salt ratio r. The registered form -ln r, from the log in SPMe's electrolyte overpotential, halves the cross-validated error (21.3 to 11.3 Wh/kg) and beats (1 − r)2 and the 0.1 flag. As a planner, fitted on 16-design pilots, it lands within 2× of SPMe's DFN cost on only 2 of 4 cycle counts. As an online correction it is slower than milestone 1's flag rule (528 against 418 s). Post hoc: SPMe@100's 14-call cost comes from the single DFN-best design, which is salt-depleted and drops from rank 1 at 10 cycles to 41 at 100. A plain whole-pool 10-cycle SPMe screen reaches a design within 1% of the DFN best in 123 s on pools of 64 and 172 s on 96, ahead of GP-EI (220 s) and every earlier screen. Exploratory: one parameter set, the same 128 designs. A research programme (proposal and log on the project page) on when a lithium-ion electrode design search can trust a reduced electrochemical model. Milestone 4b (co-kriging multi-fidelity BO) replays autoregressive co-kriging over a cheap rung (SPM or 2-cycle DFN) and 100-cycle DFN, with augmented EI (Huang et al. 2006) and an MF-UCB fidelity rule (after Kandasamy et al. 2016), on the cached benchmark with measured run times. Started from five random DFN runs (122 s), no planned variant beats GP-EI (best 204.6 against 220.4 s on pools of 64; 267.1 against 220.4 s on 96) and all are far slower than whole-pool screening on small pools (157 against 46 s at 16 designs); three pre-registered hypotheses, two refuted. Charging each design its own measured time keeps the method order (Spearman 0.90). Exploratory, chosen after the result: starting from ten 2-cycle DFN runs ties the best screen at every pool size (38, 90, 144, 174 s at 16, 32, 64, 96 designs) and beats GP-EI at each. Milestone 3 (theory, part 2a) treats the screen’s residual as independent noise and gives an exact expected count of DFN runs (a one-dimensional integral for Gaussian noise). As a planner it calls whether whole-pool screening beats GP-EI right on 14 of 16 (screen, pool size) cases, against 8 of 16 for the worst-case formula; with one whole-space noise level it ranks the 11 screens only at Spearman 0.51 (refuted), 0.86 with the noise level near the top, because SPMe’s large errors fall on particular designs (on the DFN-best ones at 100 cycles: 14 DFN runs needed, 3 predicted). Milestone 3 (theory, part 1) proves that screen-then-verify needs at most as many full DFN runs as there are designs within 2κ of the best, where κ is the screen’s worst residual after the best affine fit, so scale and shift errors are free; the bound held on all 330 (screen, pool) cases. Across 11 screens κ ranks the DFN calls needed at Spearman 0.72, the raw error at −0.07; SPM’s residual is a quarter of SPMe’s (11.0 against 42.8 Wh/kg) and SPMe’s tracks its own minimum salt concentration (Spearman −0.82). The worst-case cost formula built on it predicted screen against GP-EI on only 8 of 16 pool sizes (refuted). Milestone 4 (search replay) replays 12 search methods on the cached benchmark, 30 pools of 64 designs, each simulation charged its measured wall time: screening every candidate with the plain SPM (100 cycles) or a 2-cycle DFN run and verifying in screen order reaches a design within 1% of the best 100-cycle DFN score in a median 153 or 160 s, against 220 s for GP-EI on DFN; the 10-cycle DFN screen takes 253 s (pre-registered H7, that it would need a third of GP-EI's time, refuted), successive halving over DFN cycles 247 s (185 s if runs resume), and milestone 1's trust flag cuts SPMe screening from 700 to 418 s. On pools of 96 GP-EI catches up, so whole-pool screening suits small candidate sets. Milestone 2 (dense benchmark) runs 128 fresh space-filling (Sobol) designs for 100 cycles under SPM, SPMe and DFN (384 runs, every cycle kept): a 10-cycle DFN run ranks the designs by their 100-cycle DFN Wh/kg at Spearman 0.962 (95% 0.932–0.977), against 0.641 (0.480–0.789) for a full 100-cycle SPMe run, at the same wall time (3.6 s against 3.7 s), and its top 10 contain the DFN-best design, which SPMe ranks 41st. Unplanned: the plain SPM ranks better than SPMe (0.955; 0.984 against 0.769 over the 121 designs SPMe completes), though it over-scores the best design by 20 Wh/kg, and 15 of 128 designs (12%) are mis-scored by SPMe by over 25%. Milestone 2a, the same question on the 49 stratified designs of energy-cell-dfn: 10-cycle DFN 0.977 against 0.834 for 100-cycle SPMe (paired bootstrap difference 0.138, 95% 0.057–0.271), and a linear fade extrapolation fails (Spearman 0.01). Milestone 1: a 2-cycle SPMe run's minimum electrolyte concentration classifies the designs SPMe under-scores by more than 25% with ROC AUC 0.997 on the 49 (0.994 on the 128, whole-run minimum). Re-runs reproduce the committed SPMe and DFN scores exactly. Limits: one parameter set and protocol, costs timed on one design and one 4-core machine, no measured cell for these designs.
